els.text: A flax mill from 1840, ten minutes’ walk from Leeds station. Step-free throughout, with a quiet room and childcare on both days.
Free for students, and for anyone for whom £40 is the reason not to come. Just ask; nobody will ask why.
The first six. Eighteen more in January.

els.text: Ten minutes’ walk from Leeds station, along the canal. The doors open at nine on both days.
Step-free from the street to every room, with lifts to both floors and seats kept free at the front.
Live captions on the big screen for every talk, and a hearing loop in the Mill Hall.
Upstairs, all day, no talking. Childcare in the Loft for under-tens, free, booked with your ticket.

sections.text: Which ticket, your name, and anything we should know about access, diet or childcare. We reply within a day.

posts.title: The call for speakers is open
posts.text:
We want to hear from people who build things with WordPress every day: developers, designers, writers, the person who looks after the site at the village hall.

Talks are thirty minutes. First-time speakers get a mentor, a practice run and a coffee on us.

The call closes on 30 November. Send us an idea in a paragraph; that is all we need to start.

posts.title: Why the Old Mill
posts.text:
We looked at nine venues. The Old Mill was the only one with step-free access to every room, daylight in the main hall, and a yard big enough for six hundred people to eat lunch in.

It is also ten minutes from the station, along the canal, which is the nicest walk to a conference we know.

posts.title: Every talk will be captioned
posts.text:
This year every talk in the Mill Hall has live captions on the big screen, written by people, not software.

The captions will also go into the recordings, which go up a week after the event.
